rawFindings.title: Incorrect trust proxy invocation in req.protocol getter
rawFindings.explanation: The 'trust' function is called with only one argument (the remoteAddress) in the req.protocol getter, but it should be called with two arguments: the remoteAddress and a hops count (usually zero). This change removes the hops count argument, which can lead to incorrect behavior when 'trust proxy' is configured to trust a number of hops.
rawFindings.suggestion: Call the trust function with two arguments: trust(this.connection.remoteAddress, 0) instead of trust(this.connection.remoteAddress).
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: If 'trust proxy' is configured with a number (e.g., 1), req.protocol will ignore the hop count and may incorrectly not trust the proxy, causing the protocol to be incorrectly reported as 'http' instead of 'https' (or vice versa).
